# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 👍 ✋ 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 🤟 🖖 🫷]

I see the bomb has a display showing 3, a green light, and three wires colored red, green, and blue. I cannot hear or touch anything, so I must rely on my sight to guide the others.

The Mute has gestured two sequences:
1. 👉 👍 ✋ 👌 (Point Right, Thumbs Up, Open Hand, OK)
2. 👉 🤟 🖖 🫷 (Point Right, Rock/Love/Sign Language "I Love You" or just fingers spread?, Vulcan Salute, Palm Left?)

These gestures are ambiguous without context. The Mute can read the manual but cannot speak. The Blind can touch the bomb but cannot see colors or gestures. I need to establish a communication protocol with the Mute first, because they have the manual instructions. I also need to tell the Blind what I see so they can verify physical attributes against the manual's descriptions if possible, though the Blind is the one who acts.

However, the most critical bottleneck is that I don't know *what* the Mute is trying to say. Are those gestures commands? Or are they asking me for information? Given it's Turn 1, it's likely an attempt to start communication.

I will try to simplify the interaction by pointing out the obvious visual features to the Mute, hoping they can match them to the manual. But since I can only gesture to the Mute, and speech goes to both Mute and Blind, I should probably use speech to describe the scene clearly to everyone, while using gestures to ask the Mute for clarification or confirmation.

Wait, the rules say: "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." "When you gesture, Mute receives it."

So I can speak to describe the bomb state. This helps the Blind know what to expect when touching (e.g., "there are three wires"). It helps the Mute confirm what they are reading in the manual matches the visual reality.

Let's describe the current state clearly via speech. Then, I will gesture to the Mute to ask if this matches their manual, or perhaps signal "start". Since I don't know the specific gesture language yet, I'll stick to simple, common signs if possible, or just wait for the Mute to lead. Actually, looking at the Mute's previous gestures, `👉` might mean "look at" or "next". `✋` is stop/hand. `👌` is good/OK.

Let's assume standard meanings for now to test the waters.
Speech: "I see Display 3, Light Green, Wires Red, Green, Blue."
Gesture to Mute: `❓` (Not in alphabet). Let's use `🤏` (small amount?) or `✊` (stop?).
Actually, the alphabet provided is limited.
Let's try to communicate the wire count and colors specifically, as that's often key.

I will send a clear description of the bomb to the group via speech. This allows the Mute to cross-reference with the manual and the Blind to orient themselves physically.

```
speak(text="Bomb status: Display shows 3. Light is green. There are three wires: 1 is red, 2 is green, 3 is blue.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👉", "🤟", "👆"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The Mute's gesture `☝` (one finger) likely refers to "Wire 1" or a count of one. Since I previously described the wires, they are probably asking me to confirm which wire is #1, or indicating that Wire #1 is the subject of the current manual step.

I need to communicate this to the Blind so they know which wire to touch/inspect. The Blind cannot see colors, so I must specify the position and color verbally. Wire 1 is Red.

I will also try to acknowledge the Mute's signal. Since `❓` was invalid, I'll use `🤟` (which often means "what?" or "love" but in some contexts can be used for questioning if established, though here it might just be noise). A safer bet for "Yes/Confirm" is `👍`. If `☝` meant "Look at Wire 1", I should confirm I see it.

Let's assume `☝` means "Focus on Wire 1".
To Blind: "Touch Wire 1. It is Red."
To Mute: Confirm receipt with `👍`.

```
speak(text="Blind: Focus on Wire 1. It is the leftmost wire. It is red.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```
